title: Never Lose Writing
eyebrow: Burst A design (#163) · for approval · nothing built yet

short.lead: Text you are typing disappears because each time the app redraws the screen (a "repaint"), it rebuilds it from saved data, and half-typed text is not saved anywhere. A sync finishing, or a click that changes something else, wipes the form. The fix keeps every open form's text as a draft that a repaint puts straight back.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes and what it needs from you.
items: The whole app area is rebuilt from saved data on every repaint (app/js/app.js:286). A GitHub sync (line 1087 of the same file) and a pull from your other devices (app/js/sync.js:157) both repaint when they land. The add-task form stays open, but its boxes come back empty.
You pick the answers and approve
The three choices under Choices set how drafts behave.
Pick your answers, then send them with the words "Build plan approved: Burst A".
I build drafts for every open form
Typing copies each box into a draft. A repaint fills the boxes back in from it. The draft is also kept on this device, so a reload or a closed app keeps it too.
I prove it in a real browser
A test types into a new task with steps, triggers a sync and a click elsewhere, then checks that every character is still there, at phone width and on a wide screen.
Start a task with steps, wait for a sync or switch apps and come back, then click elsewhere.
About two minutes in the app.

changes: keep
Repaints that wait for a drag
A drag in progress already holds back repaints until it ends.

The same idea protects the Board and project dragging today (app/js/app.js:276). Drafts use the same idea of protecting your work, but they do not hold repaints back, so sync results still show straight away.
keep
The project search box
Already keeps its place and cursor across a repaint.
The search box puts its cursor back after a repaint (app/js/app.js:283). Drafts extend that to every box in an open form.
new
Drafts for open forms
Every box in an open form is copied as you type and filled back in after a repaint.

This covers the add-task form, the task editor (title, steps, due date, priority, labels) and the project editor, plus the Sort screen's note editor if you pick option A (every form) in the third choice. A draft ends only when you save or cancel it.
A repaint empties any form you are typing in.
A draft per open form, refilled on every repaint and kept on this device.
Nothing you type is lost to a sync or a stray click.

Clicking away from a new task
Your answer to the first choice below ("What should clicking away from a half-made task do?") decides what happens.
The text is lost
The text is kept
Today a click that repaints anything else wipes the new task's boxes. This is the issue "Clicking off a task being created discards it" (#157).
chg
Saving after a sync changed the same task
Your save wins.
A sync could land on top of what you are editing
What you typed is saved over the sync's change

When you save, your version is the newest. So when devices combine their data one record at a time, yours is kept on every device. A sync never edits a draft. This follows the issue "Syncing must not overwrite a thought mid-write" (#155).
choices: clickaway
What should clicking away from a half-made task do?
A
Keep it open as a draft
The form stays where it is with your text and steps, marked Draft, until you save or cancel it.
B
Save it as a task straight away
If it has a title, it becomes a real task with its steps. Without a title it stays a draft.
C
Keep it as a draft, but fold it away
The form closes, and "+ Add task" shows a Draft mark; opening it brings your text back.
Option A (keep it open as a draft) is the least surprising: nothing is created that you did not mean to create, and nothing is hidden.
escape
What should Escape do in the add-task form?
A
Close it, keep the draft
Reopening "+ Add task" brings the text back. Cancel still throws it away.
B
Close it and throw the text away, as now
Option A (close it, keep the draft) is safer: Escape is easy to press by accident, while Cancel is a deliberate tap.
where
Which forms get drafts?
A
Every form: add task, edit task, edit project, and the Sort screen's note editor
One rule everywhere.
B
Only adding and editing tasks
Adding a task and editing a task, the two places the Burst A issues describe.
Option A: one rule is easier to trust than a list of places where it applies.

wrapup.summary: A design to stop syncs and stray clicks wiping text you are typing, by keeping every open form's text as a draft.
wrapup.changing: Two new files (the draft store and its tests) and changes to the app's input, save and cancel handling. Nothing changes in sync or GitHub code.
